rules.rule: Review the logical change, not only the diff. Before commenting on lines, reconstruct what the pull request is supposed to accomplish from its title, description, and the issue it references, then check the implementation against that intent. Raise a top-level comment when a requirement or acceptance criterion stated in the issue or the description is not implemented. End each such comment with a short direction to the PR author: either fix it in this PR or create a follow-up issue, and inform the product team about any scope changes.

mirrord-protocol is primarily the protocol between the mirrord CLI (layer and intproxy) and the agent, and we try hard to keep it operator agnostic. Flag any new message or variant that only the operator sends or handles. Ask the PR author to justify it in the description: why it can't reuse existing messages, and why it can't live in the operator's own API instead. Accept a convincing justification; without one, suggest a more generic message or moving the logic to the operator.
Before accepting a new helper, trait, module, or codepath, check whether an existing abstraction already covers it and request extending that instead.

A change in behavior can make pages false that it does not touch ("Changes That Reach Several Pages" in docs/AGENTS.md). When a PR changes what a config field, CLI flag, or Helm value does, search docs/docs/ for it and flag each page outside the diff that still describes the old behavior. When a PR adds a database engine or queue service, flag each list of its siblings it is missing from, including its row in docs/docs/reference/feature-matrix.md, the lists in docs/docs/sharing-the-cluster/queue-splitting.md, and, for an engine with a default branch image, the default images table in docs/docs/managing-mirrord/operator.md. Some lists name only a few siblings, so search for several of them.

Every fenced json or yaml code block in a markdown file must carry a tag in the fence info string from the set documented in skills/CONTRIBUTING.md. Flag any block with no tag or a tag outside the set. For blocks tagged mirrord, mirrord=<path>, mirrord-up or mirrord-up=<path>: flag the block if it is not valid JSON or YAML (placeholders like ..., inline comments, trailing commas), for a mirrord=<path> fragment flag it if <path> does not exist in mirrord-schema.json at the repository root or the block's top-level keys are not properties of the object at that path, and for a mirrord-up=<path> fragment flag it if <path> does not exist in mirrord-up-schema.json at the repository root or the block's top-level keys are not properties of the object at that path. Skip the files listed under "Exempt files" in skills/CONTRIBUTING.md.
